clue.text: How to escape paying for the eggs it produces?

definitions.text: How to escape paying for the eggs it produces?

parts.words: How to escape paying for the eggs it produces?
parts.note: to dodge a payment is to duck the bill, and the egg-laying Australian platypus is called by that same two-part name

explanation.surface: A riddle about how to get out of paying for some eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer is how to escape paying: you duck (dodge) the bill. Read as one word, it is the platypus, one of the few mammals that lay eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: The platypus, an egg-laying mammal, takes this nickname from its flat, duck-like snout.

clue.text: Its levels for comparison may be sound

definitions.text: Its levels for comparison may be sound

parts.words: Its levels for comparison may be sound
parts.note: a unit used to compare loudness, so the levels it measures are of noise

explanation.surface: A remark that some comparison scale is reliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like 'reliable' but means noise: this unit compares noise levels.
explanation.definitionFit: A logarithmic unit measures how loud a noise is relative to a reference level.

clue.text: Card-game for fellow members here

parts.note: a club is a card of one of the four suits
house, or housey-housey, is an old British name for bingo

explanation.surface: A card game laid on for fellow members of an association.
explanation.walkthrough: House (housey-housey) is an old British name for bingo. 'Card-game' looks like one thing but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A society's premises are where its members gather and socialise together.

clue.text: A sign for the rest

definitions.meaning: a zodiac sign, Libra, whose symbol is the scales
the remainder or what is left over

explanation.surface: A gesture standing in for everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: The Balance or Scales is another name for Libra, a sign of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra's emblem is the weighing scales, a zodiac sign; and what is left over after part is used is the remainder.

clue.text: Fail to get trip to Seoul?

indicators.note: to trip is to stumble, so the words to Seoul stumble into a new order

explanation.surface: Missing out on a journey to the South Korean capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' looks like a journey but is the anagram signal: it rearranges TO SEOUL.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss an opportunity is to be deprived of a chance, the phrasal verb's sense.

clue.text: Jolson rejected a head-dress made from this cloth

parts.note: Al Jolson, the American singer, gives his first name

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the words a head-dress are read in reverse order

parts.note: a cap is a simple head-dress

explanation.surface: Al Jolson turns down a hat made of a certain fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' is the reversal signal, acting on 'a head-dress' only; Al Jolson was the American singer of The Jazz Singer.
explanation.definitionFit: The fine wool of a South American animal related to the llama is woven into a soft fabric of the same name.

clue.text: Primal chaos prevailing initially in an old country

parts.note: the abyss is the bottomless chaos of the ancient creation story
in can mean current or prevailing, as in fashion

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Original disorder holding sway at the start of a former nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes I and A, the first letters of 'in an'. ABYSSINIA was the old name for Ethiopia.
explanation.definitionFit: Abyssinia was the former name of Ethiopia, a state no longer called by that name.

clue.text: Sack 'attendant with internal complaint

indicators.note: internal means the illness is placed inside the attendant

parts.note: a page is a boy attendant
an ill is an ailment or complaint

explanation.surface: Dismiss a servant who has a stomach problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' looks like 'fire' but here means plunder; 'internal' is the container signal, 'with' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunder a town violently after capture is to loot it, a verb sense of sack.

clue.text: How to injure one's neck, say, at this game?

definitions.text: How to injure one's neck, say, at this game?

parts.words: How to injure one's neck, say, at this game?
parts.note: a crick is a painful neck strain, and the bat-and-ball game starts with that word

explanation.surface: A question about getting a stiff neck during some sport.
explanation.walkthrough: A crick is a painful stiffness in the neck; the bat-and-ball sport begins with that word.
explanation.definitionFit: The English bat-and-ball sport, played between two teams of eleven, is a game.

clue.text: Old farmhand moves his empty lorry grudgingly

parts.note: a churl was a peasant or farm labourer in old English society

indicators.note: the letters of his are moved around into a new order
an emptied word keeps only its first and last letters, the middle taken out

explanation.surface: A farm worker of old shifts his lorry with no load in it, reluctantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves' turns HIS into ISH; 'empty' leaves L and Y, the first and last letters of 'lorry'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone acting in a surly, ungracious manner gives things only grudgingly.

clue.text: Retreat to opposite sides, crossing the main road

indicators.note: the left and right letters straddle the road, so they go around it

parts.note: L and R stand for left and right, the opposite sides
the A1 is Britain's main north-south road, with the 1 written as the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone falls back to either side of a busy highway.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the longest numbered road in Britain, running from London to Edinburgh; crossword setters often write it as AI.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild animal's den is the hideaway it withdraws to, a place of refuge.

clue.text: After initiating burglary, perhaps, he banked coins secretly

indicators.note: the scrambled words come after the opening letter, placing them second
initiating a word means taking just the letter it starts with
perhaps suggests one possible arrangement, so the words he banked coins are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thief who has just broken in quietly pays some coins into the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initiating' takes B from 'burglary'; 'perhaps' rearranges HE BANKED COINS into EHINDONESBACK, which comes 'After' the B.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without someone knowing, out of their sight, is the idiom's sense of covertly.

clue.text: Most obtrusive yobbo taking in some of the French

indicators.note: the lout takes the French word into himself, so it goes inside

parts.note: a yobbo is a British slang term for a lout
des is French for some (of the)

explanation.surface: A thug grabs a few French people and makes himself very conspicuous.
explanation.walkthrough: A yobbo is a British slang word for a rowdy young man; 'taking in' is the container signal, and 'some of the French' is the French word for 'some'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being the noisiest makes something the most intrusive, the hardest to ignore.

clue.text: Miser is broke, without a coin, gold having been stolen

indicators.note: without means outside, so the broke word goes around the coin

parts.note: skint is British slang for broke, penniless

indicators.note: having been stolen means the gold is taken out

parts.note: a florin was an old British two-shilling coin
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted man is penniless, with no money, his gold taken.
explanation.walkthrough: Skint is British slang for penniless; a florin was an old British two-shilling coin. 'having been stolen' leaves FLIN, and 'without' (outside) is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingy person who hates spending is a tight-fisted hoarder of money.

clue.text: Workers, maybe, belonging to splinter groups

parts.note: in can mean belonging to, as in being in a club
sects are factions broken away from a larger body

explanation.surface: Employees who are members of breakaway factions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Workers' suggests employees, but here it means worker ants or bees, which is why 'maybe' is there.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker ants and bees are examples of six-legged creatures, the 'maybe' marking them as one kind.

clue.text: Standard review aroused no anger

parts.note: crit is short for criticism, a critical review

indicators.note: aroused means stirred up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: A typical critique stirred up no fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aroused' mixes NO with a synonym for anger to give ERION.
explanation.definitionFit: A benchmark by which things are judged is a measure or test.

clue.text: Return fare covers musician carried too far

indicators.note: the reversed word wraps around the musician, one letter each side
return means the word for fare is read backwards

parts.note: to fare is to do, as in how did you fare
Giuseppe Verdi was the Italian opera composer

explanation.surface: A ticket home pays for a performer who went too far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' looks like a ticket price but is the verb, as in 'how did you fare?' = 'how did you do?'. 'Return' makes OD, and 'covers' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo something is to take it to excess, beyond reasonable limits.

clue.text: Reluctance to be without a personal account

indicators.note: to be without means to lose the letter a

parts.note: an aversion is a dislike or reluctance

explanation.surface: Someone hesitant to go without their own record of events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be without' takes the A out of AVERSION.
explanation.definitionFit: One person's telling of events is their own side of the story.

clue.text: Ruler managed to come first in classification

indicators.note: to come first places the managed word ahead of the ruler

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A ruler arranged to finish top in the table.
explanation.walkthrough: The ruler is named first in the clue, but 'to come first' moves the 'managed' word ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Placing things in order of position or grade is a form of sorting.

clue.text: Seductress — one about to become a blackmailer

parts.note: a vamp is a woman who uses her charm to exploit men
the Roman numeral I is one
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A temptress, on the point of turning into an extortionist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seductress' looks like a definition, but the definition is at the other end of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a bloodsucker is anyone who drains others of money, as an extortioner does.

clue.text: Enterprise opening on a Yorkshire river

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the opening comes first

parts.note: a vent is an opening or outlet
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A business launch beside a northern English river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a county in the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A risky business undertaking is a project or undertaking.

clue.text: Entertainment thus provided in king's place in painting

indicators.note: provided in ... place means one thing supplied where another stood
the word place completes the phrase in the king's place, a substitution

parts.note: a mural is a painting on a wall
R is the abbreviation for rex, king
sic is Latin for thus

explanation.surface: A show offered in the monarch's stead within a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided in king's place' means SIC (Latin for thus) replaces R (Latin rex, king) in MURAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage show with songs is a form of theatrical entertainment.

clue.text: One-time container, lightweight but obsolete

parts.note: ex means former or one-time
a tin is a container
ct is the abbreviation for carat, a tiny unit of weight for gems

explanation.surface: A former box, light but out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: A carat (CT) weighs only a fifth of a gram, hence 'lightweight'.
explanation.definitionFit: A species or practice that has died out completely no longer exists.

clue.text: Working frantically for set fee? No fun!

indicators.note: frantically suggests wild, disordered movement, so the words for set fee no fun are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone works at a frenzied pace for a fixed fee and hates it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frantically' rearranges FOR SET FEE NO FUN.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being extremely busy, rushed with constant tasks at work.

clue.text: State made reported payment? Gosh!

indicators.note: reported means the words are taken as heard, spoken aloud

parts.note: a fee is a payment for a service; gee is an exclamation of surprise, like gosh

explanation.surface: A country produced a report of a charge, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, FEE GEE sounds like the name of the Pacific island nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific island republic is a sovereign nation, which is a sense of the word state.

clue.text: Order given by popular union

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a junction is a joining or union of things

explanation.surface: A command issued by a well-liked trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' suggests a trade union, but it means a joining point.
explanation.definitionFit: A court ruling that tells someone to do or stop doing something is a legal command.

clue.text: Man of honour no longer at hand? But he is!

definitions.text: Man of honour no longer at hand? But he is!

parts.words: Man of honour no longer at hand? But he is!
parts.note: the honoured figure's title holds the old-fashioned word for near, spelt out in his own name

explanation.surface: A gentleman of honour seems to have gone, yet he is still around.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is on 'nigh', an old word for near or at hand: it is no longer in everyday use, yet it sits inside this title of honour (K-NIGH-T).
explanation.definitionFit: A man given an honour by the monarch, entitled to be called Sir, holds this rank.

clue.text: Spring outfit includes new compact

parts.note: a well is a spring of water

indicators.note: the outfit holds the letter for new inside it

parts.note: a kit is a set of clothes or equipment

explanation.surface: A spring wardrobe contains a new make-up compact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season and 'compact' like a powder case; they are a water source and an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A sturdy, solidly built body is described as firmly put together, dense and close-set.
